approach: Matching decompilation: C++ compiled with the original VC++ .NET 2003 compiler, each function verified byte-exact or by differential emulation against the original. The same src/ also builds as a native 64-bit port (Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS arm64/x86_64, Windows x86_64) behind a Win32/Direct3D 9/DirectInput/FMOD compatibility layer over SDL3 and Vulkan, with Jolt Physics standing in for Newton.
notes: All 3,270 game functions (static CRT excluded) have compilable source, organised as one .cpp per original translation unit. 2,183 are byte-identical to the original (66.8% of functions, 27.3% of code size); the rest are tested for equivalence by running the original and our code on the same inputs under emulation. Hybrid builds splice our non-identical functions into the original exe to playtest them. Pre-release native binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows are on the Releases page; they contain no game files and need your own copy of Mount & Blade 1.011 (Steam).
help: Matching the remaining equivalent functions byte-exact (cl 13.10 codegen: register allocation, scheduling, frame layout)
Playtesting the native port on real hardware, especially Windows and Linux GPUs/drivers beyond the Apple silicon and VMs it was developed on
